name: Rosewood Doha
positioning: Waterfront hotel in two coral-inspired towers in Lusail's Marina District, with Qatari art and culture woven through
best_for: Travelers who want hands-on Qatari culture, from falconry to a dhow lunch
Families, with the Rosewood Explorers kids programme

facts.text: Rosewood Doha is in Lusail, Qatar.
The hotel stands on the south-easterly tip of Lusail's Marina District.
The reception area displays pieces sourced from Souq Waqif, including brass-studded wooden boxes traditionally used to store a dowry.
Artworks by local creatives such as Yasser Al Mulla and Azzam Al Mannai hang on the walls.
The hotel has eight dining spaces.
Koo Madame's dining space is designed to evoke 1920s Shanghai.
Mila serves Levantine recipes on Doha's Arabian Gulf shoreline.
Stoke & Stoker pairs cocktails with Asian plates and crudo, overlooking the Gulf.
Asaya Kitchen works with local farmers, purveyors and artisans.
Junior Suites have Arabian Gulf or Lusail City views and a marble bathroom with a double rain shower.
The Reef Suite has a king bedroom, a marble bath, living and dining spaces, and butler service.
Conde Nast Traveler named Rosewood Doha to its Hot List 2026.

highlights.text: The two towers are encased in a white latticed facade inspired by the forms of a coral reef.
Guests can take pottery classes with local architect and ceramicist Reema Abu Hassan at Clay Encounters.
The hotel offers a leisurely lunch aboard a traditional dhow through Lusail's waterways, and an encounter with Qatar's art of falconry.
Afternoon tea at The Butterfly Room is bookended with a dedicated chocolate trolley.
Children are catered to through the Rosewood Explorers programme, with a dedicated kids pool, an outdoor play area and an indoor kids club.

considerations.text: The hotel is in Lusail, which is a 30-minute drive from Hamad International Airport.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the ultra-luxury positioning.
